work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXV.

items.text: Honor your father and your mother, as God commands, that your days may be long.
items.citation: Compleat Body, Sermon CLXXV
items.quote: Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVI.

items.text: Show them the honor due to them by faithfully discharging every parental duty.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVI
items.quote: PARENTS own an Honour to their Children, and they are to manifest it by the dis〈…〉ge of Parental Duties to them.

items.text: Love them with that peculiar affection which nature itself plants in a parent's heart, since God uses it to picture his own love for his children.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVI
items.quote: there is a p〈…〉cali〈…〉r Love Naturally deriving from Parents to their Children.

items.text: Obey your father and mother as long as you live, for by natural generation they have a right to govern you.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVI
items.quote: the Duty of Obedience to Parents, is inculcated from their being so, Prov. 31.2.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXV.

items.text: Maintain an inward good esteem of your father and mother and show it by outward respect, deference, and careful performance of the duties you owe them.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon 175
items.quote: not enough to maintain an inward esteem of them, but it must be manifested in a way wherein it may be duly testifi'd.

items.text: Hearken to your father who begot you, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon 175
items.quote: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.

items.text: Honor your grandparents and all ancestors in the direct line as you honor your father and mother.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon 175
items.quote: all Progenitors in a direct Line, as Grand Parents, and all ascending ... are called our Fathers and Mothers in Scripture Language.

items.text: Do not rule your children despotically, but faithfully perform the duties you owe them as their superior.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon 175
items.quote: the Duties which Superiours do owe to Inferiours; for they are no more left by the Word of God to be despotical, than the others to be disobliged.

items.text: Perform the duties of honor that belong to those of equal rank toward one another.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon 175
items.quote: there are some who stand on even Ground, and in the same Rank with others, to whom also they owe a Duty in that Order.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXXVIII.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVII.

items.text: Refuse with modesty any command that is contrary to God's revealed will.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: If Parents Command their Children that which is contrary to the Divine Precept, they are bound with Modesty to refuse Obedience.

items.text: Obey them in all that is just and good, with a willing mind and alacrity.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: They ought to Obey them in all that is Just and Good... with a willing Mind, and with all Alarity.

items.text: In things not sinful, obey without disputing while under their care and charge.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: In things that are not in themselves Sins, nor in their Circumstances, they ought to Obey without disputing, so long as they are under their Parents Care & Charge.

items.text: After marriage, keep reverence for your parents and show them due regard, though you are no longer under their servitude.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: When they are Married, tho' they owe a reverence to their Parents, yet they are at their own dispose.

items.text: In public office, follow the law of your trust; do not obey parents in anything contrary to your administration, though you may consult them for advice.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: In the discharge of Publick Trust they are bound to the Law... they are not to obey them in any thing, which is contrary to the Rule of their administration.

items.text: Keep a deep impression on your heart of your parents' just authority, even if they are poor, despised, harsh, or wicked.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: An endeavour to get and keep a deep impression upon their hearts, of the Just & Right Authority of their Parents over them.

items.text: Thank God for parents who use their authority to keep you from sin, and do not be displeased when your sinful desires are checked.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Thank God for such Parents, as carefully use their Authority, to keep them from the path of the destroyer.

items.text: If you plead with your parents about an inconvenience, do it humbly, and be ready to submit to their authority if they persist.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: humbly and submissively to plead with their Parents about the inconvenience apparent in the thing, yet withal to testify a readiness to acknowledge Parental authority, if they persist

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXIX.

items.text: Obey the mistress of the house, for she also has authority over you.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXIX
items.quote: the Mistress, who also hath power of Authority over Servants

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXX.

items.text: Carry themselves with sobriety, gravity, temperance, and soundness in faith, charity, and patience, that their age may be honored and the young may learn from them.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience.

items.text: Give civil respect and deference to the aged, honoring their gray hairs.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: God hath commanded an agreeable Deference

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXXIX.

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXIX
items.quote: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.

items.text: Honor your father and mother, for this is the first commandment with promise.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXIX
items.quote: Honour thy father and mother (which is the first commandment with promise)

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVIII.

items.text: Draw together as yoke-fellows, bearing the burdens of the family as one pair.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: they are called Yoke-fellows, and so are to draw together in the Yoke.

items.text: Submit to your husband's authority, as God has ordered a subordination in the marriage bond.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: God hath also made an imparity between them, in the order prescribed in his Word, and for that reason there is a Subordination.

items.text: Have one wife at a time, as God made one man and one woman for marriage.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: one Man was to have but one Wife at a time

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVII.

items.text: Hearken to your parents' counsels: obey their instruction and warnings, and let their authority bear weight with you.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: To remember, this I had from my Father and Mother, who loved me, and sought my good, and shall I not be careful to obey it?

items.text: Receive your parents' rebukes with submission; do not reply, but take them kindly and be more careful for the time forward.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: take reproofs kindly, and take warning by them, and be more heedful, to themselves for the time forward

items.text: Receive their corrections without rebellion, ascribing them to love, and give them reverence even when the discipline seems severe.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: We have had Fathers of our flesh, who corrected us after their own pleasure, and we gave them reverence.

items.text: Fear to offend your parents; seek to please them and avoid grieving them, and if you have grieved them, seek reconciliation.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Ye shall fear every man his Mother and his Father.

items.text: Take direction from your parents in how you spend your time; ask their leave for lawful liberties and give them a true account of your doings.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Children are not to come and go, and do as they please, but to take their direction from their Parents about it

items.text: Be content with what your parents can provide for you, and accept their allowances thankfully as from God's providence.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: accept thankfully of their love and kindness in that little which they do cheerfully allow them out of what they have

items.text: Hide your parents' infirmities, whether natural, sinful, or of old age; do not despise or reproach them for these.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Hearken unto thy Father that begat thee, and despise not thy Mother when she is old.

items.text: Take your parents' advice and consent before entering marriage, and obey their authority in this weighty change.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: if Parents have an Authoritative influence into this Affair, then Children must needs owe their Obedience in it

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVIII.

items.text: Reverence him from the heart as your superior, and let that reverence ground your subjection.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 178
items.quote: Let the wife see that she Revere her Husband.

items.text: Manage your superiority over your wife so that she may take delight in it, not account it slavery.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 178
items.quote: so managed by the Husband, as that his Wife may take delight in it, and not account it a Slavery, but a Liberty and Priviledge

items.text: Use all lawful means to oblige him, accommodating yourself to his disposition without sin.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 178
items.quote: To study & use all lawful ways to oblige him... to accommodate our selves to his disposition

items.text: Hearken to him in his lawful counsels and demands, and comply unless they contradict God's will.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 178
items.quote: hearken to him, in his lawful Counsels and Demands

items.text: Take delight in his honor as your own and uphold his reputation.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 178
items.quote: To take delight in his Honour, as her own & use means to uphold it.

items.text: Rest satisfied with his condition and be a cheerful companion to him in adversity.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 178
items.quote: To rest satisfied with, and take Content in his Condition... a cheerful Companion to him

items.text: Manage household affairs with fidelity and frugality, disposing nothing of moment without his consent.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 178
items.quote: To use Fidelity and Frugality, in managing the outward Concerns of the Family... nothing of any great moment disposed of, without his Knowledge and Approbation.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVIII.

items.text: Love her with the entire love with which Christ loved the church; manage all your authority so as to express that love, for she is your nearest companion and second self.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies: he that loveth his wife loveth himself.

items.text: Show singular tenderness to your wife, considering her as the weaker vessel, especially in childbearing and nursing.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: Shew a singular Tenderness, considering her as the weaker Vessel.

items.text: Maintain your wife's authority in the family, and do not tolerate contempt from children or servants against her; give her honour as co-heir of grace.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: maintain her Authority in the Family... both Children and Servants pay her the due respects... be severe in bearing testimony against Contempt shewn to his Wife

items.text: As head, excel in wisdom and knowledge, and dwell with your wife according to knowledge, guiding your affairs with discretion.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: dwell with them according to knowledge.

items.text: Carefully provide for your wife all things needful for her comfort, as you would your own flesh.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: laying himself out for her Comfort, that she may not want any thing that is needful

items.text: Lead your wife with pious counsel and a godly example, requiring nothing of her but what is agreeable to God's revealed will.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: lead and guide her with Pious Counsel, and a Godly Example

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXV.

items.text: Honor your father and mother with cordial respect and hearty obedience, not merely outward compliance.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 175
items.quote: Honour thy Father and thy Mother

items.text: Exercise authority over your inferiors within the bounds God has set, not arbitrarily or tyrannically.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 175
items.quote: God hath laid down Precepts in His Word, by which he hath set bounds to each of these Excesses

items.text: Be willing to bear the yoke of obedience to your superiors, not froward or refusing to be under command.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 175
items.quote: such as are in Inferior to be Froward, and not willing to bear the Yoke, or be under any Command

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXXIX.

items.text: Educate them in the fear of God, as the way to lay up blessing for them.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXIX.
items.quote: their Faithful Endeavours to Educate them in the Four of God

items.text: Honor your father and mother; do not set light by them, but carefully comply with the duties required.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXIX.
items.quote: Cursed be he that setteth light by Father or Mother

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXX.

items.text: Rise up before the aged, stand uncovered in their presence, hearken to them when they speak, give respectful answers, bear with their infirmities, and do not insult them.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God: I am the Lord.

items.text: Listen attentively to the grave discourses of the aged and pious, allowing them liberty to communicate, and do not interrupt them, thinking yourself wiser.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: Their grave Discourses are observed to be hearkened unto.

items.text: Ask counsel of aged and experienced men in matters of great moment, and do not rely on your own fancy or the counsel of your contemporaries.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: Their Counsel is to be asked in matters of great moment.

items.text: Acknowledge and imitate the good example of the aged and pious, both while they are alive and when they are dead.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: Their good Example is to be acknowledged and imitated.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVI.

items.text: Nourish them tenderly in their infancy, supplying suitable food, clothing, and protection until they can provide for themselves.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: Children are in their Minority altogether uncapable of looking after themselves... supply them with suitable Food and Raiment, watch to defend them from Mischief.

items.text: Bring them up to be fit to live in the world: teach them to read and write, and put them to an honest calling.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: Train up a child in the way he should go... see that they be taught to Read and Write... provide some honest Occupation for them.

items.text: Provide for them suitably according to their rank and your ability, and lay up a portion of your estate for their future, without partiality.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: keep a due Medium between sordid Penuriousness, and profuse Lavishness... to lay up for their Children... distribute it to them according as there is Occasion.

items.text: See that they are baptized in their infancy as a seal of initiation in the covenant of grace.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: Baptism is a Seal of Initiation in the Covenant of Grace... it is the Duty of Parents to seek this for their Children.

items.text: Instruct them early in the truths of God's word, suit the teaching to their capacity, and persuade them to seek God.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: begin betimes to instill into them the knowledge of the Truths of the word of God... use earnest endeavours to perswade them to seek God early.

items.text: Set before them a good example in both words and conduct, for children learn more by example than by precept.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: CAREFULLY to set before them a good Example, both in Words & Carriages.

items.text: Pray for them unceasingly and with importunity, carrying them to God in secret and striving for a blessing on them.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: be ever Commending them to God, by uncessant and importunate Prayer... saying as Abraham, O that Ishmael might live before thee!

items.text: Maintain your parental authority by avoiding the extremes of harshness and over-indulgence, and govern them according to their age and capacity.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: avoiding the extreams of Rigour & Indulgence... Instruction is oftner to be applied than Correction... Correction is never to be administred... in a Passion.

items.text: Regulate their works and recreations, assigning them business and not allowing them to waste their time in idleness.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: They are to set them their business, and see that they attend it... so many Children brought up in Idleness, and spend their whole time in Play.

items.text: Govern their company, restraining them from associating with evil companions that would corrupt them.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: He that walketh with wise men, shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed... My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.

items.text: Command them to attend the public ordinances of worship, and keep them from assemblies where heresy or superstition is practiced.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: he will command his Children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord... restain them from such Assemblies, where Heretical Doctrines are taught.

items.text: Exercise prudent authority in disposing them in marriage, especially forbidding them from being unequally yoked with persons of another religion.
items.citation: Willard, Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 176
items.quote: Their Advice and Direction is to be used, and their Consent is to be had ordinarily... forbidding... their being unequally yoked with Persons that are of another Religion.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXXIX.

items.text: Educate your children; do not neglect their due education.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXIX
items.quote: Do not Parents neglect the due Education of their Children

items.text: Do not rise up against your parents' government; submit to their authority.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXIX
items.quote: Children rise up against the Government of their Parents

items.text: Do not despise the aged as if you were wiser; give them honor.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXIX
items.quote: Do not Young Men Despise those that are Aged; and cast Dirt upon them, supposing themselves to be Wiser?

items.text: Discharge the duties you owe to those under your authority; do not neglect them.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXIX
items.quote: Is there not a neglect in all sorts of Superiours, in the discharge of their Duties Relative?

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVIII.

items.text: Love each other with conjugal love, as Christ loved the church and gave himself for it.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the Church, and gave himself for it

items.text: Care tenderly for one another, bear with each other's infirmities, protect health and reputation, and strive to please one another.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: They are to be very tender of each others Reputation

items.text: Endeavor to promote each other's eternal salvation by being patterns of piety, praying for one another, and quickening one another to the fear of God.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: Travail in Birth for their Conversion and Salvation

items.text: Allow your wife her God-given authority over children and servants, even while holding the headship.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: her Husband is to allow it to her

items.text: Acknowledge your husband's superiority and submit to his authority, for the marriage covenant includes his headship.
items.citation: Willard, Sermon CLXXVIII
items.quote: she in so doing takes him in that Relation which carries such a Superiority in it, and consequently engaged herself to carry it to him as so

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXXVIII.

items.text: Provide suitable maintenance for your children according to your power and ability.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: The children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

items.text: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord; give them the means of spiritual good.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, Eph. 6.4.

items.text: Exercise due government over your children; do not overindulge them or let them have their will in all things.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: there is a government of children, which belongs unto parents by a natural right.

items.text: Do not treat them with bitterness or cruelty; do not provoke them to anger, lest they be discouraged.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: Fathers: provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.

items.text: Do not command or advise them to do anything sinful.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: to be their advisers and instructors in such things as are breaches of God's holy law.

items.text: Set them a good example, not an evil one.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: Children are apt to imitate their parents, and in nothing more than in things that are evil.

items.text: Do not withhold from them seasonable marriage, either by forbidding it or withholding encouragement.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: withhold from them seasonable marriage: and that either by forbidding them, or withholding due encouragement.

items.text: Obey your parents' lawful commands.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: what their parents do lawfully command them, they cannot without sin refuse obedience unto.

items.text: Honor your father and mother; do not despise them, even when they are old.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.

items.text: Remain under family government; keep the orders of the household and do not absent yourself at will.
items.citation: Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXVIII
items.quote: They come and go when they will, keep what company they please; and absent themselves as they please.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVII.

items.text: Obey their lawful commands.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Children, obey your Parents in the Lord: for this is right.

items.text: Do not comply with their sinful commands; you are bound to obey God rather than them.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Children are bound equally with their Parents to Obey God

items.text: Provide needful succour for them in their necessity.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: affording needful Succour in their Necessity

items.text: Do not provoke them to wrath.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: provoke not your Children to wrath

items.text: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord

items.text: Instruct them in what is duty and what is sin, for they depend on you in their ignorance.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Parents Instruction to teach them what is Duty, and what is Sin

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXXIX.

items.text: Honor your father and mother, as the Lord commands, and do not break the bands of order in the world.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXXIX.
items.quote: such as break all the Bands of Order in the World

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXIX.

items.text: Honor, love, and respect all servants; the meanest has a right to it.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: there is an Honour, Love and Respect which they owe to all; and the poorest Slave has a right to it

items.text: Command nothing but what is just and lawful; never require of them what God forbids.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: They are to Command them nothing but what is just and right

items.text: Forbear scurrilous and undue threatenings; moderate your severity so as to reform, not harden, them.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: Forbear scurrilous and undue threatenings

items.text: Correct them with prudence and humanity; avoid cruelty in word or blow, and never in ungoverned rage.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: They are to Correct them with Prudence and Humanity

items.text: Allow them a full liberty to plead their innocency; inquire into the case before reproof or correction.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: Allow them a full liberty to plead their Innocency

items.text: Take care for their souls: instruct them in the fear of God, allow them the ordinances, and give them seasons for reading the Word and secret worship.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: take Care for their Instruction in the fear of God, and allow them the liberty of the Ordinances

items.text: Provide wholesome, sufficient, seasonable food, suitable apparel, and tender care in sickness; do for them what is just and equal.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: see that they have wholesome, sufficient and seasonable Food and that they have suitable Apparel to cover their nakedness and defend them from the injury of the Seasons

items.text: Reverence them with fear and trembling, as those who have authority over you.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear & trembling

items.text: Obey their lawful commands cheerfully; if they command sin, humbly refuse, but do not murmur or dispute.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again

items.text: Be diligent and faithful in your service, accounting your master's profit as your own; avoid eye-service and purloining.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: Not with eye-service, as men-pleasers, but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God free the heart

items.text: Bear hard usage patiently; do not rise up or take revenge, but commit your cause to God.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon 179
items.quote: he is not to rise up against his Master; or by any way, take his own Revenge upon him

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXVII.

items.text: Afford your parents needful succour in their necessity, remembering what they spent on you.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: Affording them needful Succours in their Necessity.

items.text: Take care of your parents so they are not a public charge.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: it is the Duty of Children, to take care of their Parents, to their Ability, that they be not a Publick Charge.

items.text: While you live with them, cheerfully spend your labor for their comfort and do not desert them while they need you.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: During their Abode with them, in a cheerful laying out their labour & endeavour, that their Lives may be comfortable.

items.text: After you have a family of your own, continue to care for them, share your portion, and deny yourself conveniences rather than let them suffer.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: yea, to deny themselves and theirs of many conveniences, rather than their own Parents should suffer.

items.text: In their sickness and old age, see that they lack no tendance or needful thing, bear with their infirmities, and avoid grieving them.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: seeing that they want neither for due tendance, or any other thing their Condition calls for; and readily bear with their Infirmities.

items.text: Give your parents a decent burial according to your ability.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: also to take care for their decent Burial, according to their Condition and Ability.

items.text: Learn first to show piety at home and requite your parents and grandparents, especially if they are widowed, so the church is not burdened.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: But if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their Parents.

items.text: Relieve widows in your own family so that the church is not charged.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: If any man or woman that believeth, have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the Church be charged.

items.text: Support a widowed mother-in-law past her labor, as Ruth supported Naomi.
items.citation: Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXVII
items.quote: no less commendable is that of Ruth, in labouring to Support her Mother-in-law, who was past her labour, and in Poverty.

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXX.

items.text: Give filial subjection to your father as the natural head of the family.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: they would have owed to him, a filial Subjection

items.text: Honor your father and mother, for the fifth commandment is a moral law engraved on your heart.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, Sermon CLXXX
items.quote: The Fifth Commandment... a Precept of the Moral Law, and engraven upon Men's Hearts

work: A Compleat Body of Divinity in Two Hundred and Fifty Expository Lectures on the
heading: SERMON CLXXXVIII.

items.text: Provide for your children; furnish them with what they need.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: Parents e...ght to ...rith their Children.

items.text: Do not take or spend your parents' goods without their leave; respect their authority over the family estate.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: Children have not the liberty to take and spend at there Pleasure

items.text: Relieve your parents in their necessity; do not harden your heart or let them perish.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: They ...arden their Hearts against them; and will rather suffer them to Perith than afford them the necessary Succours

items.text: Please one another carefully; avoid quarrels and provoking each other.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: obligeth them carefully to please one another

items.text: Uphold each other's authority in governing the family; do not contradict or undo each other's acts.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: thwarts the Duty of upholding each others Authority

items.text: Keep the marriage bond and bed undefiled; do not be false to one another.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: When they break the Marriage Bond, and defile the Marriage Bed

items.text: Love your wife as your companion; do not be bitter or insulting, nor treat her as a slave.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: Hathands, love year waves, and be not b...r against them

items.text: Submit to your husband's authority; do not usurp, despise, or insult him.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: despiseth him in her Heart

items.text: Be industrious and careful in your place; do not let things go to waste through idleness.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: She remarks not how things are Wasted; and ... ought to use Care and ... in her place

items.text: Treat your servants justly; give them fitting food and clothing, and do not overwork or beat them.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: Ma...iers, give unto ... is ... and ...

items.text: Obey your master and do your service faithfully; do not refuse his commands.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: refusing to do ... Service

items.text: Rise before the aged and honor the old; do not despise them or scorn their counsel.
items.citation: A Compleat Body of Divinity, SERMON CLXXXVIII.
items.quote: Thou shalt rise up before the hary head, and ...on...ur the fa... of the old man
